families.name: Global Fabric
families.desc: AI-ready Network-as-a-Service — offices, clouds, apps, and partners on one platform.

seller.sentence: Connect sites, clouds, and applications worldwide from one NaaS platform.
why: Multinationals stall when every region is a different network and a different contract.
Global Fabric provisions, scales, and observes connectivity on demand.
SSE, SD-WAN, and internet access sit on the same fabric instead of beside it.

next.label: Global Fabric on BT International
next.hint: NaaS platform page — footprint, demos, and how sites connect.

story.text: Sites, clouds, and partners share one software-defined fabric.
Capacity and new locations provision on demand, not as a new WAN project.
Peering into SSE choices — Cisco, Fortinet, Netskope, Zscaler.
Ops Fabric watches the same estate you just stood up.

families.name: Direct Internet Access
families.desc: Dedicated, uncontended internet for cloud, voice, and SaaS — the underlay Global Fabric and SD-WAN ride.

seller.sentence: Dedicated internet for cloud, collaboration, and the WAN that follows the application.
why: Shared broadband cannot carry voice, SaaS, and SD-WAN at once.
DIA is the access layer Global Fabric Business Internet builds on.
It is also the on-ramp for SD-WAN and hybrid work.

next.label: Direct Internet Access
next.hint: Dedicated internet, Global Fabric Business Internet, and ICR.

story.text: Uncontended bandwidth at HQ, regional offices, and remote sites.
Low-latency routes for voice, video, and Microsoft 365.
Flexible and burstable capacity as demand moves.
Global Fabric Business Internet when you want the NaaS wrap.

families.name: Internet Connect Reach
families.desc: DIA beyond BT’s own PoP footprint, delivered with local ISP partners under one BT relationship.

seller.sentence: Reach markets outside BT’s native PoPs without adding a second internet provider.
why: Coverage gaps force a second ISP and a second operating model.
ICR extends DIA through trusted local partners.
The customer still has one BT contract and one fabric story.

next.label: Internet Connect Reach
next.hint: Described on the DIA page as partner-delivered dedicated internet.

story.text: Markets beyond the native PoP footprint.
Local ISP delivery, still under BT.
Those sites feed DIA and Global Fabric like any other access.
One relationship instead of a patchwork of ISPs.

families.name: SD-WAN
families.desc: Managed SD-WAN over landline, broadband, and 4G/5G — Cisco is one of the stacks BT runs.

seller.sentence: Managed SD-WAN so branches, data centers, and cloud share one experience.
why: Hybrid work and SaaS broke the old MPLS-only WAN.
BT runs a multi-vendor managed overlay, including Cisco.
SD-WAN is the WAN half of SASE; SSE is the security half.

next.label: SD-WAN and SASE
next.hint: Managed SD-WAN, SASE, and multi-vendor support.

story.text: Choose the overlay — Cisco is one of the supported stacks.
DIA, ICR, and Global Fabric carry the packets.
Pair with SSE to make it SASE.
Single-pane visibility; Ops Fabric for the managed wrap.

families.name: SASE / SSE
families.desc: Cloud security at the edge. Global Fabric peers into Cisco Secure Access, Fortinet, Netskope, and Zscaler.

seller.sentence: SASE as SD-WAN plus SSE, with a choice of security vendors on Global Fabric.
why: Users and apps no longer live on one corporate network.
BT managed SASE pairs SD-WAN with SSE from Cisco and three other vendors.
Global Fabric peers into those SSE clouds instead of hairpinning the internet.

next.label: SD-WAN and SASE
next.hint: Managed SASE — SD-WAN plus a choice of SSE.

story.text: SD-WAN is the network half.
SSE from Cisco, Fortinet, Netskope, or Zscaler.
Global Fabric takes a short path into the vendor’s cloud.
One managed SASE service, not four DIY integrations.

families.name: Global Voice
families.desc: Global SIP, inbound contact, and UC Edge — the voice platform under calling and collaboration.

seller.sentence: One voice platform for inbound, outbound, and the UC stack that sits on top.
why: Country-by-country PBX and SIP estates do not scale.
Global Voice is the carrier layer for Webex, Teams, Zoom, and contact.
UC Edge routes the same numbers onto whichever collaboration platform the user is on.

next.label: Global Voice
next.hint: Global SIP, inbound contact, and UC Edge.

story.text: Global SIP and inbound numbers in one provider.
UC Edge sends calls to Webex, Teams, or Zoom without a port.
Fraud controls sit in the voice platform, not in each PBX.
Ops Fabric covers the voice domain with the network.

families.name: Webex Calling
families.desc: Cloud calling on Webex — from on-prem PBX to a per-user cloud service, including One Cloud Cisco.

seller.sentence: Move calling to Webex, on Cisco’s cloud or hosted in BT data centres.
why: On-prem PBX fleets are expensive to keep current across countries.
Webex Calling is the Cisco cloud path; One Cloud Cisco is BT-hosted Cisco.
Both sit on Global Voice for PSTN and on UC Edge when the estate is mixed.

next.label: Cloud collaboration tools
next.hint: Webex Calling, One Cloud Cisco, and the wider collaboration set.

story.text: Webex Calling in Cisco’s cloud, or One Cloud Cisco in BT DCs.
Global Voice provides the PSTN layer.
Webex Meetings sits next to calling in the same suite.
UC Edge if some users stay on Teams or Zoom.

families.name: Webex Meetings
families.desc: Meetings from any location and device — the meetings half of the Cisco collaboration suite.

seller.sentence: One meetings service globally, on the same Cisco collaboration path as calling.
why: Meetings fail when every region picks a different platform.
Webex Meetings is the Cisco meetings offer on the BT collaboration page.
It sits with calling and Cisco Collaboration, not as a side tool.

next.label: Cloud collaboration tools
next.hint: Webex Meetings alongside calling and Cisco Collaboration.

story.text: Meetings from any device, any location.
Webex Calling is the voice neighbour in the same suite.
DIA and Global Fabric carry the media.
Ops Fabric covers the digital-experience domain.

families.name: One Cloud Cisco
families.desc: BT-hosted Cisco voice and collaboration in BT data centres, billed per user per month.

seller.sentence: Cisco collaboration hosted in BT data centres — cloud calling without moving the stack off Cisco.
why: Some customers want Cisco UC in a BT cloud, not Cisco’s public cloud.
One Cloud Cisco is that hosted path, on a per-user commercial.
It still maps to Webex Calling and the Cisco Collaboration proposition.

next.label: Cloud collaboration tools
next.hint: One Cloud Cisco — hosted Cisco voice and collaboration.

story.text: Cisco UC in BT data centres.
Pay per user per month.
Global Voice for PSTN; UC Edge if the estate is mixed.
Same Cisco Collaboration family as calling and meetings.

families.name: Cisco Collaboration
families.desc: Meetings, messaging, and calling as one Cisco proposition on the BT collaboration page.

seller.sentence: The Cisco collaboration suite — calling, meetings, and messaging sold as one path.
why: Buying calling, meetings, and rooms as three deals fragments the estate.
BT lists a Cisco Collaboration proposition next to the Webex SKUs.
It is the umbrella over Webex Calling, Meetings, and One Cloud Cisco.

next.label: Cloud collaboration tools
next.hint: Cisco Collaboration proposition — meetings, messaging, calling.

story.text: Calling, meetings, and messaging as one Cisco offer.
Cisco cloud or One Cloud Cisco in BT DCs.
Global Voice and UC Edge underneath.
The Cisco 360 / Preferred Partner relationship on the BT Cisco page.

families.name: UC Edge
families.desc: Route calling to Webex, Teams, or Zoom on BT GSIP without porting numbers when the platform changes.

seller.sentence: Keep the numbers. Change the UC platform. UC Edge sits between GSIP and Webex, Teams, or Zoom.
why: Mergers and platform shifts usually mean number ports and downtime.
UC Edge routes to Webex, Teams, or Zoom on the same Global Voice layer.
Webex is one of the three platforms, not the only one.

next.label: Global Voice — UC Edge
next.hint: UC Edge is the flexible voice layer on Global Voice.

story.text: Numbers stay on Global Voice / GSIP.
Webex, Teams, or Zoom — without a port.
Users can change platform without a commercial reset.
SASE still covers the clients, whichever UC they use.

families.name: Ops Fabric
families.desc: AI-powered managed operations across connectivity, overlay, security, Global Voice, and digital experience.

seller.sentence: The operating wrap — observability, automation, and experts across network, voice, and security.
why: Global Fabric and Global Voice still need someone to run them.
Ops Fabric is that operating model: observability, AI, and domain experts.
It spans connectivity, overlay, network security, Global Voice, and digital experience.

next.label: Ops Fabric
next.hint: Managed operations across BT’s connectivity, voice, and security domains.

story.text: Observability across network, overlay, security, and voice.
AI-assisted insight and auto-remediation.
Operational hubs and domain experts behind the tooling.
One operating model instead of three NOCs.
